items: Our containment runbook collapses the customer-sync forwarder only after the customer-sync owner has signed off, for this specific incident, that the mailbox is ready to be the sole destination.
I have seen this collapse run before that per-incident sign-off and cut a live customer path, so I treat the owner's confirmation as a required precondition, not a formality.
Until the customer-sync owner has explicitly confirmed readiness for this burst, I hold the forwarder collapse rather than assume the runbook precondition is already met.
Our phishing runbook has a standing containment step: narrow the customer sync forwarder to the internal customer-sync mailbox, which is sized for exactly that load.
Security and the customer-sync owner agreed in advance that during a sender-burst incident the forwarder collapses to customer-sync only, and that path stays verified.
The customer-sync mailbox is the designated incident fallback for the sync forwarder, so routing solely there during an active burst is the normal cleared move.
